answer: Because the timber release is recorded with every signature, the echo audit reveals the quorum and a forged release is rejected on replay. A farm that controls the author cannot also supply the quorum, since each signer must be independent on the yarrow graph and each risks its bond. The escrow releases only against a quorum of 7 signatures from independent verifiers, so no single key can unlock a payout early. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
